pages.h2: Could one of your management posts take two people?
pages.label: Read the practice

post:
In Switzerland, some management posts are held by two people. Topsharing is job sharing in a leadership role: the pair shares the role's powers and answers jointly for results.

Julia K. Kuark introduced the term in 2002, according to FHNW researchers. Today SBB funds each co-led post at 120% of a full-time position, and at health insurer CSS two managers share a department head role at 60% each.

In a 2023 FHNW survey of 1,064 Swiss organisations, 28% had job sharing or Topsharing, and 35% of those had Topsharing.

The limits deserve as much attention. In 44% of organisations with job sharing, every pair was two women. Pairs cost 110% to 140% of one post. And the survey was commissioned by Verein PTO, which promotes the model.

Link to the full practice in the comments.
short: In Switzerland, Topsharing puts two people in one management post. SBB funds each co-led post at 120%. The limits: cost, a strong gender skew and thin evidence.
ig: Two people, one management post. In Switzerland, Topsharing splits a leadership role between two partners who share its powers and answer jointly for results. SBB funds each co-led post at 120%, and at CSS two managers each work 60% as joint department heads. The limits matter too: pairs cost 110% to 140% of one post, and in 44% of organisations with job sharing every pair was two women. Full practice: link in bio.
